chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The penalty (hadd) of the grave robber is the penalty (hadd) of the thief.'

key_terms.النَّبَّاش: Grave robber / one who digs up graves
key_terms.حَدّ: Fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal penalty for a grave robber?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal equivalence between grave robbers (al-nabbash) and thieves (al-sariq), applying the standard hadd of amputation for theft to the act of digging up graves. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the sanctity of the grave and the severity of violating it, treating the removal of the body or grave goods as a distinct form of theft warranting the same corporal punishment. The narration, transmitted through the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, highlights the practical application of Quranic penal codes to specific social contexts in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibraahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Penalty (Hadd) of the grave robber is the Penalty (Hadd) of the thief’.
